mainTopic: The permanent exemption of כהנים and לויים, the Levite lambs that redeemed firstborn donkeys in the מדבר, and the מחלוקת of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש on whether בכורות in the מדבר were holy
overview: First the גמרא learns from the word וְהָיוּ that כהנים and לויים stay exempt from בכורה in every generation, not just in the מדבר. Next it asks how we know the Israelites' firstborn donkeys in the מדבר were redeemed with a שה. רב חסדא's comparison to כסף is rejected, and a verse that joins בכור אדם with בכור בהמה טמאה proves it instead. רבי חנינא adds that one Levite lamb exempted many donkeys. אביי and the wording of the verse (בהמת versus בהמתם) prove this, and רבא shows it is the reason behind the משנה that one lamb may redeem many times. Then רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about whether בכורות born in the מדבר were holy. They test each side against sources about firstborns serving before the משכן, the offerings on the day the משכן was set up, and a בריתא about three places of holiness. Finally, רב פפא's verse about counting the firstborns forces a new version of the dispute: both agree the בכורות in the מדבר were holy, and they argue whether that holiness continued. ריש לקיש's side of this version is finished on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Where do we learn the exemption applies for all generations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that כהנים and לויים are exempt from בכורה in later generations too, not only in the wilderness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for later generations, how do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. We already know the Levites were exempt from בכורה in the desert, but how do we know this still applies in future generations?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses in במדבר describe a one-time exchange of the לויים for the firstborn in the wilderness. So one could think the exemption was only for that generation. The גמרא wants a source that it is permanent.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And for later generations, from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the earlier discussion of the wilderness exemption to future generations.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source that the exemption of כהנים and לויים from בכורה is permanent.

steps.title: The word 'shall be' means they stay as they are
steps.stepSummary: The verse וְהָיוּ לִי הַלְוִיִּם teaches that the לויים remain in their status forever, so the exemption continues in every generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And the Levites shall be Mine.' 'Shall be' means they will remain in their existing state.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a verse. The word וְהָיוּ ('they shall be') tells us the לויים will stay the way they are now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The form וְהָיוּ suggests something lasting, not a one-time event. So the status the לויים had in the desert, including exemption from בכורה, carries forward to all generations.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall remain in their (current) state

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And the Levites shall be Mine"
"Shall be" means they shall remain in their state.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word וְהָיוּ shows the לויים keep their status permanently, so they stay exempt from בכורה in all generations.
steps.whatToRemember: The exemption of כהנים and לויים from בכורה is permanent, learned from the word וְהָיוּ.

steps.title: How do we know the donkeys were redeemed with a lamb?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רב ספרא's claim that the Levites' lambs (שה) redeemed the Israelites' firstborn donkeys in the wilderness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know it was done with a lamb?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. Earlier (4a) רב ספרא said the Levites' lambs took the holiness off the Israelites' firstborn donkeys, and now the גמרא asks how we know it was a lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses in the desert only say the Levites' animals replaced the Israelites' animals. They don't clearly say a lamb was used for the donkeys. So a source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A lamb or kid (sheep or goat)

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it was with a lamb?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts to a new question about רב ספרא's statement on 4a.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the redemption of firstborn donkeys in the wilderness was done with a שה.

steps.title: Silver and lamb are both mentioned for later generations
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא points out that both כסף (for a firstborn son) and שה (for a firstborn donkey) are written in the Torah as permanent laws. This sets up a comparison between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: 'Silver' is stated for later generations, and 'lamb' is stated for later generations.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא begins his answer by placing silver and lamb side by side. This step sets up the comparison he will finish in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silver is the permanent way to redeem a firstborn son (five shekels). A lamb is the permanent way to redeem a firstborn donkey. Because both are permanent redemption laws, רב חסדא will compare them.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the author of this answer
Silver: the five shekels used to redeem a firstborn son

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda says:
"Silver" is stated for later generations,
and "lamb" is stated for later generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא נֶאֱמַר כֶּסֶף לְדוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sets up a comparison between כסף and שה, since both are permanent redemption laws.

steps.title: Like silver, the lamb was used both then and later
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא completes the comparison. Silver was used for redemption both in later generations and in the wilderness, so the lamb was also used in both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as silver, stated for later generations, was used to redeem in later generations and was also used at that time, so too the lamb, stated for later generations, was used to redeem in later generations and was also used at that time.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא finishes his proof. Silver worked both in the desert and afterward, so a lamb must also have worked both in the desert and afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the desert, the extra Israelite firstborn sons with no Levite to replace them were redeemed with five shekels of silver, the same as later generations. By comparison, the firstborn donkeys in the desert were redeemed with a lamb, the same as later generations. This is how we know the Levites' lambs were used.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as ... so too (a comparison formula)

phrases.english: Just as silver, which is stated for later generations:
they redeemed with it in later generations,
and they redeemed with it at that time,
phrases.notes: The surplus firstborn in the desert were redeemed with five shekels (במדבר ג:מז).

phrases.english: so too the lamb, which is stated for later generations:
they redeemed with it in later generations,
and they redeemed with it at that time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison set up in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That the firstborn donkeys in the wilderness were redeemed with a שה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to כסף, which was used for redemption both in the wilderness and in later generations.

steps.title: Silver is special because it redeems other holy things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's comparison. Silver has a wider power of redemption, since it also redeems הקדש and מעשר שני, so it cannot teach about a lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about silver? It is special, because consecrated property and second tithe can be redeemed with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's comparison. Silver is stronger than a lamb, so what is true of silver may not be true of a lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silver can redeem many things, such as הקדשות and מעשר שני, while a lamb cannot. Since silver is a uniquely powerful redeemer, its use in the wilderness may not prove that the weaker lamb was also used there. This kind of challenge is called a פירכא: it shows the two items being compared are not truly alike.

keyTerms.meaning: What about X? It is special because... (a formula that breaks a comparison)
Second tithe, which can be redeemed with money

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying a lamb can't redeem a firstborn donkey. It only says the comparison to silver fails, because silver has extra powers that a lamb lacks.

phrases.english: What is notable about silver?
That one can redeem with it
consecrated property and second tithe!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison made in steps 4 and 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's comparison between כסף and שה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כסף has a broader redemptive power (it redeems הקדשות and מעשר שני) that שה lacks, so a law about silver cannot be applied to a lamb.

steps.title: A new verse links the firstborn person and the firstborn donkey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops רב חסדא's comparison and brings a verse that places the firstborn person and the firstborn impure animal side by side. This shows that the lamb, like silver, was used both in the wilderness and in later generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse says: 'Yet you shall surely redeem the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of the impure animal you shall redeem.' Just as with a firstborn person you made no difference between later generations and that time, since it was always with silver, so too with an impure animal, make no difference between later generations and that time, since it is always with a lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: The previous comparison was rejected, so the גמרא brings a better source. The Torah mentions the firstborn person and the firstborn impure animal together in one verse, so they follow the same pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weakness in step 6 was that silver is a stronger redeemer than a lamb, so the two could not be compared. Now the link does not come from comparing the two redeeming items. It comes from the verse joining the two firstborns together. Since the firstborn person's redemption was the same then and later, the firstborn donkey's redemption must also be the same then and later, meaning a lamb.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Drops the previous answer and brings a new one.
The verse says. Introduces a source from the Torah.
An impure (non-kosher) animal, here meaning the donkey
For that time, meaning in the wilderness

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the accepted source that a lamb redeemed the firstborn donkeys in the wilderness. It replaces the comparison to silver that was rejected.

phrases.english: Rather, the verse states:
"Yet you shall surely redeem the firstborn of man,
and the firstborn of the impure animal you shall redeem."
Just as with a firstborn person you did not distinguish

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְדוֹרוֹת בֵּין לְאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה — בְּכֶסֶף,
phrases.english: between later generations and that time, since it is with silver,

phrases.aramaic: אַף בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה לֹא תַּחְלוֹק בּוֹ
phrases.english: so too with an impure animal, do not distinguish in it

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְדוֹרוֹת בֵּין לְאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה — בְּשֶׂה.
phrases.english: between later generations and that time, since it is with a lamb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב חסדא's comparison, which step 6 rejected, with a verse that joins the two firstborns.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a new source (the verse placing the two side by side) in place of the rejected comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lamb's use in the wilderness could be learned by comparing it to silver.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse that joins the firstborn person and the firstborn impure animal teaches that the lamb was used both then and later.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse that places בכור אדם next to בכור בהמה טמאה teaches that, just as a firstborn son was redeemed with כסף both in the wilderness and later, a firstborn donkey was redeemed with שה both then and later.

steps.title: One Levite lamb exempted many donkeys
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says that a single lamb belonging to a Levite exempted several firstborn donkeys of the Israelites in the wilderness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: One lamb of a Levite exempted several firstborn donkeys of the Israelites.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement about how the wilderness exchange worked. It was not one lamb for one donkey. One lamb covered many donkeys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we only learned that a lamb was used. רבי חנינא adds the ratio. A single Levite lamb was enough to exempt many Israelite firstborn donkeys at once, which is different from the later rule of one lamb per donkey.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
One lamb of a Levite
exempted several firstborn donkeys of the Israelites.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the fact that a lamb was used and adds how many donkeys each lamb covered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the wilderness, one Levite lamb exempted many Israelite firstborn donkeys.

steps.title: אביי's proof: the Torah counts extra people but not extra animals
steps.stepSummary: אביי supports רבי חנינא. The Torah lists the extra Israelite firstborn people who needed silver, but it lists no extra animals. So the Levite lambs covered all the donkeys.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Know that this is true, because the verse counted the extras among people, but it did not count extras among animals.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a proof for רבי חנינא. If any donkeys had been left over, the Torah would have counted them, just as it counted the extra firstborn people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were more Israelite firstborn people than Levites, and the Torah counts that surplus because those extras had to pay silver. The Torah gives no such count for animals. אביי concludes there were no leftover donkeys, because each Levite lamb covered several of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Know that this is so. Introduces a supporting proof.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Know that this is so,
for the verse counted the extras among people,
but it did not count extras among animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a proof for רבי חנינא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's claim that one Levite lamb exempted many donkeys
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse's silence: it counts surplus firstborn people but no surplus animals

steps.title: Maybe the Israelites simply had few animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's proof. Perhaps there was no surplus only because the Israelites did not have many animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps they did not have very many animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי. There could be a different reason the Torah lists no extra animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed that no surplus means each lamb covered many donkeys. But if the Israelites owned only a few donkeys, the Levite lambs could have matched them one for one with nothing left over. That would explain the silence without proving רבי חנינא.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this?

phrases.english: From where do you know this?

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא לָא הָוֵי נְפִישִׁי לְהוּ בְּהֵמוֹת טוּבָא?
phrases.english: Perhaps they did not have very many animals?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning behind אביי's proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's conclusion drawn from the missing count of extra animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another explanation fits the facts: with only a few Israelite animals, a one-for-one exchange would leave no surplus to count.

steps.title: The Israelites had huge herds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that idea. The Torah says בני ראובן and בני גד had a great amount of livestock.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not think so! For it is written: 'And the children of Reuben and the children of Gad had a great amount of livestock.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a verse showing that the Israelites owned many animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Israelites had large herds, they must have had many firstborn donkeys. So the lack of a surplus cannot be explained by a small number of animals, and אביי's proof stands again.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not think so. A strong rejection of an idea.

phrases.english: Do not let this enter your mind!
For it is written: "And a great amount of livestock belonged
to the children of Reuben and the children of Gad."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disproves the challenge's assumption from a verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the Israelites had few animals, so no surplus was left.
steps.terutzMaskana: They had large herds, so the missing surplus must mean each lamb covered many donkeys.

steps.title: Maybe the Levites' ordinary animals matched the donkeys
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. Even with large Israelite herds, maybe the Levites' ordinary, non-firstborn animals were enough to match the Israelite firstborns one for one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps even so, the ordinary animals of the Levites stood against the firstborns of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second way to explain the missing surplus. The Levites could have had enough ordinary animals to cover every Israelite firstborn, one each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Israelites had many animals, but only some were firstborn. The Levites could use any of their ordinary animals, which might have equaled the number of Israelite firstborns. Then a one-for-one exchange would leave no surplus, and רבי חנינא would still be unproven.

phrases.english: Perhaps, even so,
the ordinary animals of the Levites stood
opposite the firstborns of Israel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer in step 11 but raises a new way to explain the missing surplus.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Many Israelite animals does not mean many firstborns. The Levites' ordinary animals could have covered them one for one.

steps.title: The singular word shows one animal for many
steps.stepSummary: The verse says בהמת הלוים, a singular word, in exchange for בהמתם, a plural word. This shows one Levite animal stood in for many Israelite animals, confirming רבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And the animal of the Levites in exchange for their animals.' One animal in exchange for many animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge directly from the wording of the verse, reading the singular בהמת as 'one animal' against many. The next step challenges this reading, and step 15 defends it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah describes the Levites' animal in the singular and the Israelites' animals in the plural. That wording shows the exchange was one Levite animal for many Israelite animals, not one for one. This rules out the idea of a one-for-one match and confirms רבי חנינא.

keyTerms.meaning: In place of, in exchange for

steps.whatToRemember: In the wilderness, the Israelites' firstborn donkeys were redeemed with Levite lambs. This is learned from the verse joining the firstborn person and the firstborn donkey. One Levite lamb covered many donkeys, as the singular בהמת versus the plural בהמתם shows.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this idea stayed only in the wilderness. רבא shows that the later משנה, which lets one lamb be used to redeem firstborn donkeys many times (buying it back from the כהן each time), rests on this same principle: one Levite lamb exempted many donkeys.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And the animal of the Levites in exchange for their animals,"
meaning one animal in exchange for many animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְאֶת בֶּהֱמַת הַלְוִיִּם תַּחַת בְּהֶמְתָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12 and confirms רבי חנינא's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the precise wording of a verse (singular versus plural)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps the Levites' ordinary animals matched the Israelite firstborns one for one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse's singular and plural wording shows one Levite animal for many Israelite animals.

steps.title: Maybe the singular word means a large group
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the singular word בהמת might just be a collective word that means many animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the word means 'many animals,' as in the phrase בהמה רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 13. Maybe the singular word does not mean one animal at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 relied on בהמת being singular, meaning one Levite animal. The גמרא points out that Hebrew sometimes uses a singular noun for a whole group, like בהמה רבה, 'many animals,' in יונה. If that is the meaning here, the verse could mean many Levite animals, and the proof for רבי חנינא falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Many animals (a singular word used for a group)

phrases.english: But say it means 'many animals'?
phrases.notes: Taken from Jonah 4:11, where the singular בהמה refers to many animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the singular-word reading used in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בהמת הלוים means one animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A singular noun can be collective, so the word may still mean many Levite animals.

steps.title: The mixed singular and plural wording proves one covered many
steps.stepSummary: If both sides were meant the same way, the verse would have used matching words. The mismatch shows that one Levite animal covered many Israelite animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the verse should have written either 'animal for animal' or 'their animals for their animals.' Why write 'animal of the Levites for their animals'? Learn from this that one covered many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It points to the contrast between the two words in the same verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בהמת were a collective word for many animals, the Torah would have used the same style on both sides, either singular-singular or plural-plural. Instead, it pairs a singular with a plural. That deliberate mismatch teaches חד פטר טובא: one Levite lamb exempted many Israelite firstborn donkeys.
steps.whatToRemember: The verse pairs a singular (בהמת) with a plural (בהמתם). This shows that one Levite animal redeemed many Israelite firstborn donkeys, which supports רבי חנינא.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write
either 'animal in exchange for animal'
or 'their animals in exchange for their animals'!
What is the point of 'the animal (of the Levites) in exchange for their animals'?
Learn from it: one exempted many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual precision: the contrast between the two words is deliberate
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בהמת might be a collective word meaning many Levite animals
steps.terutzMaskana: The singular-versus-plural contrast proves that one Levite animal covered many Israelite ones

steps.title: רבא finds support in a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says a משנה already teaches that one lamb can be used to redeem firstborn donkeys many times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We also learned this in a משנה: 'And he may redeem with it many times.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a second support for רבי חנינא, this time from a משנה instead of a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that if the כהן gives the lamb back, the owner may use that same lamb again to redeem another firstborn donkey, many times over. This matches רבי חנינא's idea that one lamb can exempt many donkeys.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (in a משנה)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Rava said: We too have learned it:
'And he may redeem with it many times.'
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה later in the מסכת (9a).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a משנה-based support after the verse-based proof
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's rule that one lamb exempts many firstborn donkeys
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: ופודה בו פעמים הרבה

steps.title: רבי חנינא was explaining the reason behind the משנה
steps.stepSummary: Since the משנה already says this, רבי חנינא was not adding a new rule. He was giving the reason behind the משנה: one Levite lamb exempted many Israelite donkeys.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חנינא is explaining the reason of the משנה. This is what he is saying: Why may one redeem with it many times? Because one lamb of a Levite exempted several firstborn donkeys of Israelites.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: if the משנה already teaches this, what did רבי חנינא add? He supplied the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the practical rule, that one lamb can be reused. רבי חנינא gives the historical source for that rule: in the מדבר, one Levite lamb redeemed many Israelite donkeys. So the משנה and רבי חנינא fit together rather than repeating each other.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what he is saying

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא's statement is the reason behind the משנה's rule that one lamb may redeem many times.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥanina is explaining the reason of the mishna,
and this is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא פּוֹדֶה בּוֹ פְּעָמִים הַרְבֵּה?
phrases.english: What is the reason one may redeem with it many times?

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּשֶׂה אֶחָד שֶׁל בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: Because one lamb of a Levite

phrases.aramaic: פּוֹטֵר כַּמָּה פִּטְרֵי חֲמוֹרִים שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: exempts several firstborn donkeys of an Israelite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי חנינא relates to the משנה cited in Step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting a statement as the reason behind an earlier source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא's statement might seem to just repeat what the משנה already says
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חנינא is giving the reason behind the משנה's rule

steps.title: Were firstborns in the מדבר holy?
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens. רבי יוחנן says firstborns born in the מדבר became holy, and ריש לקיש says they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי יוחנן says firstborns in the מדבר were made holy. ריש לקיש says firstborns in the מדבר were not made holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion by quoting a מחלוקת between two אמוראים. This sets up the next steps, which give each side's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the קדושה of firstborns, both people and animals, already applied during the forty years in the מדבר. רבי יוחנן says it did. ריש לקיש says it did not, so firstborns born there had no קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)

phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
Firstborns in the wilderness were sanctified,
and Reish Lakish says:
Firstborns in the wilderness were not sanctified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic after the רבי חנינא discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחלוקת: רבי יוחנן says firstborns in the מדבר had קדושה; ריש לקיש says they did not

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's source: 'Sanctify to Me every firstborn'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's reason is that the Torah commanded the firstborns to be made holy, as the verse says קדש לי כל בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says firstborns in the מדבר were made holy, because the Merciful One said they should be made holy, as it is written: 'Sanctify to Me every firstborn.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the first side of the מחלוקת. It gives רבי יוחנן's source from a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The command קדש לי כל בכור (שמות יג:ב) was given right before the Jews left מצרים. Since the מצוה was already in force, רבי יוחנן holds that firstborns born afterward in the מדבר had קדושה.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא repeats רבי יוחנן's line on purpose. This time it is not restating the מחלוקת but beginning his proof.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: קָדְשׁוּ בְּכוֹרוֹת בַּמִּדְבָּר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Firstborns in the wilderness were sanctified,
because the Merciful One said they should be sanctified,
as it is written: 'Sanctify to Me every firstborn.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יוחנן's side of the מחלוקת in Step 18
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that firstborns in the מדבר had קדושה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse קדש לי כל בכור (Exodus 13:2)

steps.title: ריש לקיש's verse: firstborn holiness began only in the Land
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש proves from the order of the verses that firstborns born in the מדבר were not holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Firstborns in the wilderness were not made holy. The verse says 'And it shall be when He brings you' into the land, and right after that it says 'You shall set apart' the firstborns. This shows that before then, they were not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives ריש לקיש's source for his side of the argument, which was opened in Step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The command to set apart firstborns comes right after the words about entering ארץ ישראל. So ריש לקיש reads it as a מצוה that starts only after entering the Land. That means firstborns born in the מדבר had no holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall set apart (the firstborns to ה׳)
And it shall be when He brings you (into the Land)
By implication; we can infer that

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש agrees that the firstborns in מצרים were holy. He only says that the ones born in the מדבר were not holy.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
The firstborns in the wilderness were not made holy,
since it is written: 'And it shall be when He brings you,'
phrases.notes: שמות יג:יא, about entering the Land of Canaan.

phrases.english: and it is written after it: 'And you shall set apart,'
which implies that before that, they were not holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: לֹא קָדְשׁוּ בְּכוֹרוֹת בַּמִּדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Matches Step 19. רבי יוחנן gave his verse there, and here ריש לקיש gives his.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that firstborns born in the מדבר were not holy
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order of the verses in שמות יג:יא–יב: entering the Land, then 'וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ'

steps.title: Objection: before the משכן, the firstborns did the service
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a משנה that says firstborns did the עבודה before the משכן was set up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן objected to ריש לקיש: Until the Mishkan was set up, private altars were allowed, and the service was done by the firstborns!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's view with a משנה about the time in the מדבר before the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says firstborns did the עבודה in the מדבר before the משכן. Doing עבודה requires holiness. So firstborns in the מדבר must have been holy, which seems to go against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him from a source

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
Until the Mishkan was set up,
private altars were permitted,
and the service was done by the firstborns!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view ריש לקיש just stated.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that firstborns in the מדבר were not holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Firstborns did עבודה in the מדבר before the משכן. That shows they had holiness in the מדבר.

steps.title: Answer: the משנה means the firstborns who left Egypt
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the firstborns who did the עבודה were the ones born in מצרים, not the ones born in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It means those firstborns who left Egypt.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the objection by explaining which firstborns the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש already agrees that the firstborns in מצרים were holy. So the firstborns doing עבודה were the ones who came out of מצרים. That does not prove anything about babies born later in the מדבר.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It refers to those who left Egypt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's objection from Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the משנה is about a specific group of firstborns
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to show that firstborns born in the מדבר were holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is only about firstborns born in מצרים, and ריש לקיש agrees they were holy.

steps.title: Logic supports the answer: a one-year-old cannot serve
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs ריש לקיש's answer: a firstborn born in the מדבר would be less than a year old before the משכן was set up, too young to do עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. Because if you do not say this, can a one-year-old baby do the service?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds its own logical support to ריש לקיש's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משכן was set up about one year after leaving מצרים. Any firstborn born in the מדבר before then was a baby. A baby cannot do עבודה, so the firstborns in the משנה must have been born in מצרים.

keyTerms.meaning: This also makes sense; logic supports this

phrases.english: This also makes sense,
for if you do not say so,

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן שָׁנָה בַּר מֶיעְבַּד עֲבוֹדָה הוּא?
phrases.english: is a one-year-old able to do the service?
phrases.notes: The משכן was set up within a year of leaving מצרים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens ריש לקיש's answer from Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's answer that the משנה means firstborns who left מצרים
steps.raayaSupportSource: Simple logic: a baby born in the מדבר could not do עבודה before the משכן was set up

steps.title: Why did רבי יוחנן raise this objection at all?
steps.stepSummary: Since the answer is so obvious, the גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן brought this objection in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who asked it, why did he ask it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן raised such a weak objection. The next step explains what was really bothering him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 showed that the firstborns in the משנה had to be born in מצרים. So the objection seems pointless. The גמרא assumes רבי יוחנן must have had a stronger point in mind, and it goes looking for it.

keyTerms.meaning: And the one who raised this question

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new attack on ריש לקיש. It questions why רבי יוחנן made his objection, since the answer looks so obvious.

phrases.english: And the one who asked it, why did he ask it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the logic of Step 23 to ask why the objection in Step 21 was raised at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a baby obviously could not do עבודה, the משנה clearly means firstborns born in מצרים. So why did רבי יוחנן think it was a challenge to ריש לקיש?

steps.title: What really bothered רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's real point was this: if the קדושה of בכורות stopped in the מדבר, it should also have stopped for the firstborns born in מצרים. Then they could not have done the עבודה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was his difficulty: It works if you say their holiness did not stop, because then the original (Egypt-born) firstborns also kept their holiness. But if you say their holiness stopped, then the original ones should also have lost their holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 24. רבי יוחנן was not asking about the desert-born firstborns. He was asking about the ones born in מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's logic is all-or-nothing. If the rule of firstborn holiness 'switched off' in the מדבר, it should switch off for everyone, including the Egypt-born firstborns. Yet the משנה says firstborns did the עבודה. So the holiness must not have stopped at all.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what was bothering him
From the start, the original ones

phrases.english: This is what was difficult for him:
It works out if you say
that their holiness did not stop,
then those from the beginning (born in Egypt)
also did not lose their holiness.
But if you say
that their holiness stopped,
then those from the beginning
should also have lost their holiness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24's question about why רבי יוחנן objected at all.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן seemed to be asking about desert-born firstborns, which would be an obvious mistake.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was asking about Egypt-born firstborns: if the holiness stopped, it should have stopped for them too.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: whoever was holy stays holy
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that those already made holy in מצרים stayed holy. Only those who were never holy did not become holy in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (ריש לקיש) says: Whoever became holy stays holy. Whoever did not become holy does not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש pushes back against רבי יוחנן's all-or-nothing reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stopping the rule in the מדבר means no new firstborns became holy. It does not take away holiness that already existed. So the Egypt-born firstborns could still do the עבודה.

phrases.english: And the other (Reish Lakish) says:
Those who became holy stay holy;
those who did not become holy are not holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reasoning of step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the assumption that stopping new holiness cancels existing holiness.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן's logic mixes up 'no new holiness' with 'losing holiness that already exists.'
steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, in the מדבר no new firstborns became holy, but those holy from מצרים stayed holy.

steps.title: Challenge from the offerings on the day the משכן was set up
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a בריתא: on the day the משכן was set up, the people offered many קרבנות, including animal בכורות. That seems to show that animal firstborns were holy in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: On the day the משכן was set up, the Jewish people offered vow offerings and gift offerings, sin offerings and guilt offerings, firstborn animals and tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש with a new source about animal firstborns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If firstborn animals were brought as קרבנות in the מדבר, then firstborns must have been holy there. That goes against ריש לקיש's view that firstborn holiness stopped in the מדבר.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him from a source
When the משכן was set up

phrases.english: He challenged him: On that day that the Tabernacle was set up,
the Jewish people offered on it (on that day)
vow offerings and gift offerings,
sin offerings and guilt offerings,
firstborn animals and tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion about human firstborns, רבי יוחנן brings a new challenge about animal firstborns.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that firstborns in the מדבר were not holy.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Animal בכורות were offered in the מדבר, so firstborn holiness must have been in force there.

steps.title: Those were animals from מצרים
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the בכורות offered that day were animals that came out of מצרים, which were already holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is talking about those that came out of Egypt.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש uses the same answer he gave before (step 22): the firstborns in question came from מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals born as firstborns in מצרים were already holy, and holiness does not go away (step 26). So offering them in the מדבר does not prove that new desert-born firstborns were holy.

phrases.english: Here too,
it is talking about those that came out of Egypt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בכורות offered were born in the מדבר.
steps.terutzMaskana: They were animals born in מצרים, already holy before the מדבר.

steps.title: The wording 'that day' supports ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא itself supports ריש לקיש: it says בכורות were offered on that day, which suggests that afterward they were not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we can learn it from the בריתא itself: on that day they were offered, but from then on they were not offered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the wording of the בריתא backs up ריש לקיש's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בריתא mentions only 'that day.' This makes sense if a limited group of Egypt-born firstborns was offered at the start and no new holy firstborns came later. So the בריתא fits ריש לקיש's view.

keyTerms.meaning: And from it (the source itself) we can see

phrases.english: And from it we see: it was on that day that they were offered,
but from then on they were not offered!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 28.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's answer that only Egypt-born firstborns were offered.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The precise wording 'אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם' in the בריתא.
steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, the בריתא about the day the משכן was set up ends up supporting ריש לקיש.

steps.title: Second version: ריש לקיש attacks רבי יוחנן from the same בריתא
steps.stepSummary: In another version, ריש לקיש is the one who brings the בריתא. He argues that 'that day' means בכורות were offered only then and not afterward, so desert-born firstborns were not holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: ריש לקיש challenged רבי יוחנן: On the day the משכן was set up, the Jewish people offered vow and gift offerings, sin and guilt offerings, firstborns and tithes. On that day, yes. From then on, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the same discussion, with the roles switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the same inference from 'that day' that supported ריש לקיש is used as an attack on רבי יוחנן. If firstborns stayed holy in the מדבר, they should have been offered later too, not just on that day.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same בריתא and the same inference, told in a different version where ריש לקיש asks the question instead of רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Reish Lakish challenged Rabbi Yochanan:
On that day that the Tabernacle was set up,
the Jewish people offered
vow offerings and gift offerings,
sin offerings and guilt offerings,
firstborn animals and tithes.
On that day, yes;
from then on, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of steps 27-29, with the roles reversed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that firstborn holiness continued in the מדבר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The בריתא says בכורות were offered only 'that day,' so later desert-born firstborns were not holy.

steps.title: Read it as 'from that day onward'
steps.stepSummary: The answer for רבי יוחנן is to read the בריתא as saying all these קרבנות were offered from that day onward, not only on that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: from that day onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by explaining the בריתא's wording differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בריתא is not limiting the offerings to one day. It marks when they began. So בכורות continued to be offered afterward, and that fits רבי יוחנן's view.

phrases.english: Say: from that day onward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'That day' means starting from that day and continuing afterward.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides read the same בריתא differently. ריש לקיש says 'only that day,' and רבי יוחנן says 'from that day onward.'

steps.title: What is the בריתא teaching according to רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the בריתא's words 'that day' come to teach, if רבי יוחנן reads it as 'from that day onward.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is it teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. If the בריתא means the קרבנות were offered 'from that day onward' (as רבי יוחנן said), what new point is it making? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 31, רבי יוחנן read 'that day' as 'from that day on.' But then the words seem to add nothing. The גמרא needs to show that the phrase still teaches something real.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is it teaching us? (What new point is being made?)

phrases.english: And what is it teaching us?
phrases.notes: Asked on רבי יוחנן's reading of 'that day' as 'from that day onward.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the new reading from Step 31 by asking what the phrase 'that day' contributes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What חידוש the בריתא teaches if 'that day' means 'from that day onward.'

steps.title: Obligatory offerings could not be brought on a private altar
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא teaches that before the משכן these obligatory קרבנות were not brought, because obligatory offerings were never offered on a במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From that day on, yes, they were offered. Before that, no. This shows that obligatory offerings were not brought on a private altar (במה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The בריתא is teaching that obligatory קרבנות, like בכורות, only began to be offered once the משכן was set up. Before that, they could not be offered on a במה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי יוחנן's view holds together. The בכורות born in the מדבר were already holy, but they could not be offered until there was a משכן, because a במה only takes voluntary offerings. So 'from that day' marks when offering began, not when holiness began.

keyTerms.meaning: At first, before that (here: before the משכן was set up)
Obligatory offerings (like a בכור), as opposed to voluntary ones
A private altar used outside the משכן or מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the בכורות became holy only on the day the משכן was set up. According to רבי יוחנן they were already holy. They simply could not be offered until then.

phrases.english: From that day onward — yes, they were offered,
but before that — no.
This shows that obligatory offerings were not brought on a private altar.
phrases.notes: Only voluntary offerings could be brought on a במה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase teaches that obligatory קרבנות began only with the משכן, because they could not be offered on a במה.

steps.title: A בריתא: firstborns were made holy in three places
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a בריתא saying בכורות were made holy in מצרים, in the מדבר, and on entering ארץ ישראל. This seems to support רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: You end up saying that in three places the firstborns were made holy for ישראל: in מצרים, in the מדבר, and when ישראל entered the land. In מצרים, what does the פסוק say? 'Sanctify to Me every firstborn.' In the מדבר it says: 'For every firstborn among בני ישראל is Mine.' On entering the land it says: 'And it shall be when He brings you... and you shall set apart.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source. This בריתא says clearly that בכורות were holy in the מדבר too, which seems to prove רבי יוחנן right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש holds that בכורות born in the מדבר were not holy. This בריתא lists the מדבר as one of the places where they were made holy, and it backs that up with a פסוק. So it looks like a direct proof against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (the גמרא is bringing a source as a proof)
You end up saying (a summary statement)

phrases.english: Come and hear: you end up saying:
in three places the firstborns were made holy for Israel —
in Egypt, in the wilderness, and when Israel entered the land.
In Egypt, what does the verse say?
"Sanctify to Me every firstborn."
In the wilderness it says:
"For every firstborn among the children of Israel is Mine."
About their entry into the land it says:
"And it shall be when He brings you... and you shall set apart."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first בריתא was resolved both ways, a new source is brought.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that בכורות born in the מדבר were holy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A בריתא listing the מדבר among the three places where בכורות were made holy.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: they were commanded, but did not actually become holy
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the proof. He reads the בריתא as listing three places where they were commanded about בכורות, not three places where the בכורות actually became holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: In three places they were commanded about the firstborns, to make them holy, but they did not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק pushes back on the proof. He says the בריתא only lists places where a command was given. It does not say the holiness actually took effect there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a command was given in the מדבר but did not take effect there, ריש לקיש's view still stands. The proof depended on 'were made holy' meaning actual holiness. רב נחמן בר יצחק reinterprets it as 'were commanded.'

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת הוּזְהֲרוּ עַל הַבְּכוֹרוֹת לִיקְדַּשׁ,
phrases.english: in three places they were commanded about the firstborns, to make them holy,
but they did not become holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 34.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference that the בריתא shows actual holiness in the מדבר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The בריתא may describe commands given, not holiness that actually took effect.

steps.title: But in מצרים they were certainly holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק: we already said the בכורות in מצרים were holy, even according to ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in מצרים too they were not holy? But we said that they were holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading. If no holiness took effect in any of the three places, that would include מצרים, and everyone agrees the בכורות there were holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, even ריש לקיש admitted that בכורות from מצרים were holy. That was the basis of his answer in Step 28. So a reading that says 'they did not become holy' in all three places cannot be right.

phrases.english: And in Egypt too they were not holy?
But we said that they were holy!
phrases.notes: See Step 28: even ריש לקיש agrees about the בכורות from מצרים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in Step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading that no holiness took effect in the three places.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Holiness in מצרים is agreed on by all, so the reading proves too much.

steps.title: In some places they became holy, in some they did not
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק clarifies: in all three places they were commanded, but only in some of them did the holiness take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: some of them became holy, and some of them did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא refines רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading. In מצרים and in ארץ ישראל the בכורות became holy. In the מדבר they did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the reading fits what everyone agrees about מצרים, and it still keeps ריש לקיש's view about the מדבר. The command was given in all three places, but holiness only took effect in two of them.

phrases.english: This is what he means:
in some of them they became holy, and in some of them they did not.
phrases.notes: Holy in מצרים and ארץ ישראל, not holy in the מדבר.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר: מֵהֶן קָדְשׁוּ, וּמֵהֶן לֹא קָדְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 36.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No holiness took effect in any of the three places.
steps.terutzMaskana: Holiness took effect in some places (מצרים, ארץ ישראל) but not in the מדבר.

steps.title: רב פפא: the פסוק shows firstborns were counted in the מדבר
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא objects: the תורה commands counting every firstborn male in the מדבר, so they must have been holy there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא challenged this: And in the מדבר they did not become holy? But it is written: 'Count every firstborn male of בני ישראל'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the idea that the בכורות in the מדבר were not holy. He brings a פסוק showing that the firstborns in the מדבר were counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This counting took place in the second year after leaving מצרים, so it included firstborns born in the מדבר. Counting them in order to redeem them through the לוים shows they had holiness. That contradicts ריש לקיש's view as explained by רב נחמן בר יצחק.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa challenged this:
And in the wilderness they did not become holy?
But it is written:
"Count every firstborn male of the children of Israel"!
phrases.notes: במדבר ג:מ. The counting was in the second year, so it included firstborns born in the מדבר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 37 that בכורות in the מדבר were not holy.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בכורות in the מדבר did not become holy.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק commands counting the firstborns in the מדבר, which shows they were holy.

steps.title: Restating the מחלוקת: everyone agrees they were holy, but did the holiness stop?
steps.stepSummary: Because of רב פפא's challenge, the גמרא restates the מחלוקת. Both agree the בכורות in the מדבר were holy. רבי יוחנן says that holiness never stopped. ריש לקיש says they were holy, but only for a limited time (his words continue on the next עמוד).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: רבי יוחנן said: they became holy and it did not stop. And ריש לקיש said: they became holy...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier version of the argument and gives a new one. Now both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש agree the בכורות in the מדבר became holy. They argue only about whether that holiness continued.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's פסוק forces everyone to admit holiness in the מדבר. So the מחלוקת moves from 'were they holy?' to 'did the holiness last?' רבי יוחנן says it never stopped. ריש לקיש's view (it lasted only until the counting) is finished on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (the גמרא is restating a dispute)

steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת is no longer about whether בכורות in the מדבר were holy. Both sides agree they were. The question now is whether that holiness continued (רבי יוחנן) or stopped (ריש לקיש).
steps.confusionAlert: This passage ends in the middle of ריש לקיש's words. Do not assume he simply agrees with רבי יוחנן. His statement continues with a limit on the holiness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This restatement replaces the whole earlier version of the dispute, so the rest of the sugya must be read through this new framing.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: קָדְשׁוּ וְלֹא פָּסְקוּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: they became holy and the holiness did not stop,
and Reish Lakish said: they became holy
phrases.notes: His statement continues on the next עמוד: holy only until a certain point.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב פפא's challenge by reworking the entire מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both agree the בכורות in the מדבר were holy. רבי יוחנן says the holiness never stopped. ריש לקיש says it was holy, with a time limit (continued on the next עמוד).
